stem: Other company insiders have recently offered testimony that ____ several of the more lurid anecdotes found in Belmer’s account, though that testimony hardly minimizes the company’s culture of malfeasance and mismanagement.
Cells (i) ____ glucose if they are (ii) ____ it, but conversely they destroy glucose-creating enzymes upon return to glucose-replete conditions.

Often evasive and at times even (i) ____, the gubernatorial candidate came off (ii) ____ at her press conference today in ways that should give voters cause to (iii) ____ her, regardless of whether they agree with the substance of her views.

items.answerReviewReason: 校对认为配套答案不可靠
items.explanation: 配套答案为 空(i) C mendacious、空(ii) B convincingly、空(iii) B champion。前半句说她闪烁其词甚至说谎，后面“不论是否认同她的观点”都应让选民有理由拒绝她，更合理的是 空(i) C mendacious、空(ii) A badly、空(iii) A reject。

stem: A prospective reader may well wonder whether the book would not be better classified as a somewhat unorthodox biography, but the author stands firm on its status as a work of fiction. She has drawn inspiration from the facts, the author tells us, but has (i) ____ them, editing and rearranging events. Also, she has felt free to (ii) ____ what her characters were feeling and what was going on in their minds—to invent, within the limits of plausibility, what could not be (iii) ____.
One of the reporter’s central themes is that health care concerns were a secondary consideration to the reformers in their drive to limit if not completely ____ the consumption of cigarettes.

Because the fundamental nature of language is so intangible, because there is no agreed-upon way to determine its existence, it is easy to dismiss new evidence of ostensible animal language as inadequate—quite ____, but insufficient.
Whether the film is ____ adaptation of the legend is debatable: the author of the screenplay claims that it was based on the original tale, but admits taking some interpretive license with the story.
